memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Joshua returned with all Israel to the camp at Gilgal. Now the five kings had fled and hidden in the cave at Makkedah. When Joshua was told that the five kings had been found hiding in the cave at Makkedah, he said, "Roll large rocks up to the mouth of the cave, and post some men there to guard it. But don't stop; pursue your enemies! Attack them from the rear and don't let them reach their cities, for the Lord your God has given them into your hand." — Josh 10:15-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The five kings, once so proud and threatening, now flee and cower in a cave. What a reversal. The mighty rulers who had gathered to crush Gibeon are reduced to hiding in the dark, hoping simply to survive. Their alliance and their armies could not stand against the God of Israel.

Notice Joshua's wise leadership here. He orders the cave sealed and guarded, but crucially he says, "But don't stop; pursue your enemies!" He would not let the capture of the kings distract from the larger task. There was still a battle to finish. Joshua understood that a partial victory, if we grow complacent, can slip away. He pressed on until the work was complete.

There is a lesson here about not stopping short. When God gives us a measure of victory over some struggle or sin, the danger is that we relax too soon, satisfied with partial progress, and let the enemy regroup. Joshua's wisdom was to keep pursuing until the victory was thorough. In our spiritual lives, too, we are called not to make peace with the remaining enemy but to press on.

Notice again the anchor for all of it: "the Lord your God has given them into your hand." Joshua's urgency to pursue flowed not from anxiety but from confidence in God's promise. Because the victory was assured, he pursued it wholeheartedly. In Christ, we fight from victory, not merely for it, for He has already triumphed (Col 2:15). That assurance should make us press on all the more, refusing to stop short of all God intends.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you tend to relax too soon after a partial victory, letting old struggles return?
2. Where might God be calling you to "keep pursuing" rather than stopping short?
3. How does fighting from Christ's assured victory change the way you press on?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me from stopping short after partial victories. Give me the resolve to press on, confident that You have already secured the triumph in Christ. Amen.
